journey:dali-christ-of-saint-john-of-the.t: Christ of Saint John of the Cross
journey:dali-christ-of-saint-john-of-the.l: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow, Scotland
journey:dali-christ-of-saint-john-of-the.noimg: © Salvador Dalí, Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí. View at Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow.

x.summary: Dalí shows the crucified Christ from high above, as if seen from the Father's point of view, hanging in a dark sky above the calm bay of Portlligat. There are no nails, blood or crown of thorns; the body is serene, strong and suspended in a triangle of light. The striking viewpoint came from a small 16th-century drawing by the Spanish mystic Saint John of the Cross, and in 2006 the painting was voted Scotland's favourite painting.
facts: Glasgow Museums bought the painting in 1952 for £8,200, a sum that caused controversy at the time.
In 1961 a visitor attacked the canvas with a stone and tore it; it was carefully restored.

Dalí wrote that the image first came to him in a 1950 'cosmic dream' in which it represented 'the nucleus of the atom'; to study the pose he had a Hollywood stuntman, Russell Saunders, suspended from an overhead gantry.
